rp-wet-01.back: CWH, Coastal Western Hemlock: mean about 2,228 mm, range 1,000 to 4,400 mm.

rp-wet-03.back: Interior cedar and hemlock zone, the Interior wet belt: most productive Interior forest.

rp-wet-04.front: Why is dense second growth poor deer feed?
rp-wet-04.back: In the pole stage, crowded trees overtop and shade out shrubs and herbs.

rp-wet-05.front: How does old growth help coast deer in snow?
rp-wet-05.back: Crowns intercept snow, and broken branches and lichens give forage.

rp-wet-06.back: Douglas fir, western redcedar, red huckleberry, salal, deer fern, tree lichens.

rp-wet-07.back: Grasses, trailing blackberry, fireweed, pearly everlasting, forbs, and leaves of willow, salmonberry, salal and maple.

rp-wet-08.front: Most common big mammals of the CWH?
rp-wet-08.back: Black tailed deer, black bear, grizzly bear, gray wolf.

rp-wet-09.front: Where do coast black bears den?
rp-wet-09.back: Mostly in or under big trees, snags, logs or stumps.

rp-wet-10.back: Leathery, sharply toothed, egg shaped evergreen leaves 3 to 9 cm; thickets.

rp-wet-11.back: Stems armed with yellow spines 5 to 10 mm long. Do not grab it.

rp-wet-12.front: Where to sit in thick coast cover at dusk?
rp-wet-12.back: On the edge where timber meets a cutblock or opening, wind to you.

rp-wet-14.back: About 82 cm a year at the Haney station; it usually melts fast.

rp-wet-15.front: Roosevelt elk on the coast eat?
rp-wet-15.back: Sedges, grasses, ferns, plus willow, elderberry, blueberry, cedar and hemlock browse.

rp-wet-16.front: First check before any Mission area spot?
rp-wet-16.back: The Region 2 No Shooting areas in the Rule Book.
